notes: Biggest lift: prop-with-interaction (100% vs 20%). Baseline wrote a single top-down view, actively suppressed shadows, and had no red-arrow annotation - the three field-tested prop rules are exactly what the baseline lacks.

location-generate-vs-skip (100% vs 50%): baseline independently made the correct skip decision for the beach, but never specified a 3/4 angle and had no physical-coherence QA - the two platform-specific rules carried the delta.
character-with-group (100% vs 75%): baseline was strong (turnaround sheet on gray, goblin lineup) but split the face close-up onto a separate sheet, violating the one-sheet reference principle.

NON-DISCRIMINATING: librarian-register-elements passed 5/5 in BOTH configs. The baseline invented an arguably richer registry (JSON + versioning). Assertions test generic asset-tracking competence, not the skill-specific conventions (single MANIFEST.md, exact table format, draft/final lifecycle). Consider tightening assertions or accepting that the skill adds format-consistency value not captured by these checks.

BARELY DISCRIMINATING: planner-script-breakdown (80% vs 80%). Both configs failed the pigeon-flock group-variation assertion - but the with-skill run failed it by DESIGN (skill correctly says generic real-world swarms need no variation sheet). The assertion contradicts the skill and should be fixed in iteration 2, which would put with-skill at 100%.
Time/tokens: with-skill runs averaged ~50s / ~33.8k tokens vs baseline ~53s / ~32.1k tokens - the skill costs essentially nothing extra and slightly reduces wall time (less approach-invention).
Single run per configuration - treat per-eval deltas as directional, not statistically robust.
